newsitem.title: UK: Energy sees no regulatory reason to stop bid.
newsitem.headline: Energy sees no regulatory reason to stop bid.

text.p: British electricity company The Energy Group Plc does not see any regulatory reasons for the new Labour government to block a 3.7 billion stg bid it has agreed with U.S.-based PacifiCorp, executives told a press conference on Friday.
"There is no change to competitive structures so it's difficult to see why the change in government should change matters," chief executive of the group's Eastern unit said.
The bid by PacifiCorp, at 690 pence per share plus a 5.5 pence dividend, was announced earlier on Friday but regulatory worries have kept Energy Group's shares at a larger than normal discount.
At 1310 GMT, Energy shares were up six pence to 654 pence, off a high of 663 pence.

The new Labour government, which took power with a huge majority in a general election on May 1, had been fiercely critical of the previous government's stance on takeovers, which saw all but one of 12 privatised regional electricity companies (Rec) taken over in less than two years.
It also has privatised utilities in its sights for a one-off tax on excess profits which will be a central plank of its first budget on July 2.
The Energy Group, spun off from once-mighty industrial conglomerate Hanson in February, itself bought Rec Eastern Electricity in 1995.
"Eastern has already been through the process," Energy Group chairman Derek Bonham said, adding that meant ring fencing of the business was already in place.
Bonham said Devaney had already approached regulators and ministers concerned on an informal basis over the bid.
The government's proposed tax had been taken into account when calculating the bid, PacifiCorp chief financial officer Richard O'Brien said, but declined to give specific details.
"We have given it our best estimate and included it in calculations," he said.
